first.text:
Keep the swings where they are, on Monday, and put the circuit on Wednesday after the pull-up session. Here is the reasoning, day by day.

**Swings on Monday.** Monday is your lightest lifting day, about 53 of its 75 minutes, so a 12 to 16 minute swing block fits with room to spare. The swings are a hinge at an easy effort, and the day after Sunday's deadlift and hip thrust that works as a flush rather than more damage. Friday's Romanian deadlift is then four days away, so nothing hinge-heavy stacks. The other hinge days rule themselves out: Friday already has the RDL, Saturday is the day before the deadlift, and Sunday is the deadlift itself plus a run.

**Circuit on Wednesday.** Wednesday is the shortest session of the week, about 39 of its 75 minutes, so the 16-minute circuit still leaves it well under the cap. The pull-up work is all upper back and arms, and the circuit brings squats, push-ups and swings, so it rounds the day out without doubling anything. Thursday's rest then sits between the circuit's goblet squats and Friday's back squat, and the ring push-ups are three days clear of Saturday's bench. The one cost is that your legs will have done a little work before the lunchtime run, but at an easy run pace that is not a problem.

**Why not the other days.** Tuesday is the PT's. Thursday is your only full rest day, and sleep has been the thing that costs you sessions, so I would protect it. Saturday and Sunday already carry a 90-minute lift and a run each; adding a circuit there is where the week would start to get missed.

So the week reads: Monday lift plus swings, Tuesday PT, Wednesday lift plus circuit plus run, Thursday off, Friday squat, Saturday bench and run, Sunday deadlift and run.

Right now the plan fixes the swings to Monday but leaves the circuit floating for whenever you fit it in. If you want Wednesday written in so it shows up in Hevy each week, that is a small program change and I can draft it. Otherwise just do it on Wednesdays and it will count all the same.
